title: WSS draft method enumeration inconsistent: redundant ReadPosition/set, omits Chat/typing
description:
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-wss-00.md, line 113

Current text:

  All JMAP Chat owner-facing methods defined in {{JMAP-CHAT}} — including all `/get`, `/set`, `/query`, `/changes`, `/queryChanges`, `Space/join`, and `ReadPosition/set` methods — operate over the {{RFC8887}} WebSocket transport without modification.

Two issues:

1. `ReadPosition/set` is redundant: it is a `/set` method, already covered by the 'all `/set` methods' clause earlier in the same sentence. Mentioning it explicitly adds no information.

2. `Chat/typing` is omitted: it is a non-CRUD-shaped owner-facing method (signature: takes chatId + typing boolean, returns accountId; does not store anything). The leading clause 'All JMAP Chat owner-facing methods' technically covers it, but the explicit enumeration of non-standard shapes singles out only `Space/join`, creating the impression that the list is complete.

Editorial fix options:

(a) Add `Chat/typing` to the enumeration and drop the redundant `ReadPosition/set`:

  All JMAP Chat owner-facing methods defined in {{JMAP-CHAT}} — including all `/get`, `/set`, `/query`, `/changes`, `/queryChanges`, `Chat/typing`, and `Space/join` methods — operate over the {{RFC8887}} WebSocket transport without modification.

(b) Drop the explicit callouts entirely; the leading clause already covers everything:

  All JMAP Chat owner-facing methods defined in {{JMAP-CHAT}} operate over the {{RFC8887}} WebSocket transport without modification. This includes all `/get`, `/set`, `/query`, `/changes`, and `/queryChanges` method shapes.

Option (a) is more concrete; option (b) is more durable as the method list evolves. Either is acceptable.

Pure editorial; no wire-protocol or interop impact.
acceptance_criteria:
- Either Chat/typing is included in the explicit enumeration, OR the enumeration is replaced with a more durable phrasing
- ReadPosition/set is either dropped (redundant) or the choice to keep it is justified (e.g., by emphasizing its role in chat UX)
- After the fix, the reader cannot reasonably conclude that Chat/typing is excluded from WebSocket transport support
